question: A data team needs to process ten thousand support tickets overnight, where each ticket requires Claude to call tools on a remote MCP server to look up account history before drafting a response, and they want to minimize cost by processing everything asynchronously in bulk. Which setup fits this requirement?
options: A) Run each ticket through the Claude Code CLI in a for-loop, since the CLI batches requests automatically to reduce overall cost.
B) Use the Agent SDK's session resume feature to process all ten thousand tickets sequentially inside one long-running session.
C) Configure the MCP server with defer_loading enabled, which activates a built-in nightly batch-processing mode on Anthropic's infrastructure.
D) Submit requests through the Message Batches API with mcp_servers included, since MCP tool calls there price the same as regular Messages calls.
correct_answers: D) Submit requests through the Message Batches API with mcp_servers included, since MCP tool calls there price the same as regular Messages calls.
explanations: Incorrect. Looping the CLI over each ticket runs requests sequentially and interactively; the CLI has no automatic batch-pricing mode.

Incorrect. Session resume continues one conversation's context; processing ten thousand independent tickets sequentially in one session is not what it is designed for and would not reduce cost the way batching does.
Incorrect. defer_loading only controls when a tool's description is surfaced to the model; it does not enable any batch-processing mode.

Correct. mcp_servers can be included in Message Batches API requests, and MCP tool calls made through batches are priced the same as in regular Messages API calls, fitting the async, cost-sensitive overnight workload.
